description: Classifying a SERVICE response. The distinction that matters for funds is definitive-rejection versus ambiguous-outcome: a parsed {"status":"ERROR"} means the request was processed and refused, while a transport failure, an unparseable body, or a 200 that does not confirm means the mutation MAY have landed - and for rotate/split/merge the WALLET-generated secrets are then the only copy of the outputs, so they must ride the error rather than be discarded. A confirmed mutation missing a signature the output or caller requires is its own outcome: it definitely landed, so the secrets matter more than ever. `op` says which call each case is driven through - a melt is the one mutation with no signature to return.

outcomes.unverifiable: the mutation is confirmed but an output came back without its cs1 certificate, which a SERVICE MUST return for every note it issues, a bearer note included (luds fd80cdd). The note EXISTS at the output the WALLET disclosed, so keep its secret even while reporting the missing proof
outcomes.pending: this k1 has another operation in flight (a melt); retry shortly
outcomes.spent: the SERVICE is authoritative that the note is already burned; a holder may lock it as spent
outcomes.unknown: the SERVICE does not recognise this note; surface it, do not silently lock it
outcomes.error: definitively rejected for some other stated reason
outcomes.ambiguous: the outcome is not known - preserve any fresh secrets

cases.name: success without a certificate
cases.why: every output is owed a cs1 certificate in c, a bearer note included (luds fd80cdd); without one the note it names cannot be verified offline. The note exists at the output the WALLET disclosed

cases.name: a split that certifies only its first output
cases.why: the change is owed its certificate in c2 exactly as the first output is in c; the change is not a lesser note

cases.name: melt success with its verify
cases.why: OK on a melt means the payment is in flight, NOT that the note is confirmed spent. A melt mints nothing, so it has no signature to return; it carries LUD-21 verify (luds fd80cdd), which the WALLET follows to settled or Not found instead of repeating its spend

cases.name: melt success with an echoed pr
cases.why: an echoed pr is harmless and ignored

cases.name: melt success without verify
cases.why: a melt MUST carry verify, but the OK still confirms the melt was accepted: the payment is in flight either way. Reading it as an error would have the holder retry a melt that landed; the WALLET has to follow it with the informational GET instead

cases.name: pending
cases.why: the exact reason string LUD-25 specifies for a k1 mid-melt

cases.name: already in use
cases.why: the exact reason LUD-25 fixes for a spend that opens a burned note at the callback

cases.name: unknown note
cases.why: the exact reason LUD-25 fixes for a note the SERVICE never credited (luds fd80cdd)

cases.name: ambiguous callback wording is treated as spent
cases.why: an atomic multi-k1 callback cannot say which k1 failed; the spent reading is the safe one

body.reason: This mint is sunsetting - splits are disabled.

cases.name: 200 with neither OK nor ERROR
cases.why: the mutation was not confirmed and may still have landed
